adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — State-changing toggle on an unauthenticated-by-token GET with no CSRF/confirmation means email link prefetchers and corporate link scanners silently mute or unmute topics for logged-in users.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, reachable via new GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`). That action immediately mutates state by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` and `save!` based solely on `current_user` cookies (no CSRF protection/POST requirement, no confirmation step before changing state). Therefore any automatic GET fetch (prefetchers/link scanners) can silently mute/unmute a topic for a logged-in user just by visiting/scanning the URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by` can return nil (user never visited/tracked the topic, or a different logged-in user opens the link) and `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError 500.

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — Toggle semantics are wrong for "unsubscribe": watching/tracking becomes regular (still emailed for replies/mentions) instead of muted, and a second click (or scanner + user) flips regular to muted or muted stays muted, so the action is not idempotent and the page's "you will stop receiving notifications" text can be false.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code toggles `TopicUser.notification_level` based on current state: if `tu.notification_level > :regular` it sets to `:regular`, else it sets to `:muted`. This means a user who was tracking/watching will be downgraded to `regular` (not muted) on the first “unsubscribe” click, contradicting the new copy that says they “will stop receiving notifications” and making the action non-idempotent (a second request can change `regular` -> `muted`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so no MessageBus notification_level_change is published and notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at are not updated, leaving open tabs stale and audit fields wrong.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code mutates `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly. In the same diff, `TopicUser.change` clearly contains logic to publish a `MessageBus` event when `attrs[:notification_level]` is set (`MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)`). Since `unsubscribe` does not call `TopicUser.change`, no `notification_level_change` event will be published, so other open clients/tabs relying on that bus message won’t be updated in real time. The finding’s extra claims about specific audit fields (`notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at`) are not verifiable from this diff, but the MessageBus part is directly supported by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5 — Client-side navigation to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (back button, pasted link in a loaded app) only fetches the topic JSON and never hits the server toggle, yet the template still claims notifications were stopped.

adjudication.rationale: The Ember route `topic-unsubscribe` (new file `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`) defines a client-side route for `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` and its `model(params)` only does `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` then `topic.updateFromJson(json)`; it never requests the server `topics#unsubscribe` endpoint that actually performs the toggle (`TopicsController#unsubscribe` changes `TopicUser.notification_level` and calls `perform_show_response`). Because the SPA route will intercept in-app navigation/pasted links, the UI/template (`templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` rendering `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` which states notifications will stop) can be shown without the server-side toggle occurring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:102 — 301 (permanent) redirect for slug mismatch/blank slug is cached by browsers, so a later slug change or a json client following the cached redirect gets a stale URL; a 302 was intended here.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a 301 redirect in `TopicsController#unsubscribe` when `slugs_do_not_match` or (for non-JSON) `params[:slug]` is blank: `redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301`. However, nothing in the diff demonstrates that this is incorrect or that a 302 "was intended"—301 redirects for canonical slug URLs are common/intentional, and the claimed browser-caching/stale-URL breakage is speculative and not verifiable from the shown changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:101 — For json requests with a blank slug the redirect is skipped, so `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe.json` performs the toggle and returns the full topic view, another silent state-changing GET surface.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the redirect guard is `if slugs_do_not_match || (!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?)`. For the no-slug route (`get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`), `params[:slug]` will be blank. For JSON requests (`/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe.json`), `!request.format.json?` is false, so the blank-slug branch does not trigger and the action proceeds to mutate state (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`) and then calls `perform_show_response`, which includes a `format.json` response returning the topic view. This is a verifiable state-changing GET reachable via JSON without the slug redirect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — Logged-out email recipients hit `ensure_logged_in` and get a 403 instead of being redirected to login and back to the unsubscribe page, so the link from the email fails for the common logged-out case.

adjudication.rationale: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action assumes an authenticated user but does not show any explicit login requirement/redirect in this diff. It uses `current_user` immediately (`TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` and especially `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)`), which will blow up or be blocked when the recipient is logged out. So an email unsubscribe link hit by a logged-out user will fail unless some external filter handles it. The finding’s specific claim about `ensure_logged_in` returning a 403 isn’t directly shown, but the core “logged-out link fails” behavior is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:1852 — Any caller passing `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` now raises I18n MissingInterpolationArgument; other locales lack the new placeholder so non-English users never see the per-topic link.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb#html_part`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it unconditionally calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` with `template_args` built from defaults + `@opts`. There is no default/fallback for `unsubscribe_url`, so any existing call site that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does not pass `unsubscribe_url` would trigger `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at runtime. (The claim about other locales not being updated is not verifiable from this diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:107 — List-Unsubscribe header still points only at user preferences, so mail clients' native unsubscribe does not use the new per-topic URL.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show or modify the code that builds the `List-Unsubscribe` header in `lib/email/message_builder.rb` (only `@template_args` formatting and `html_part` substitution are shown). While the diff adds an `unsubscribe_url` option and uses it in the email body via `unsubscribe_link` translation, there is no diff-grounded evidence that the `List-Unsubscribe` header “still points only at user preferences” or that it fails to incorporate the new per-topic URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 — Triple-stache renders fancyTitle unescaped; safe only as long as fancy_title stays server-sanitized.

adjudication.rationale: The new template uses triple-stache: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3). That value is built in the new controller via `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`, and the translation string contains HTML (`{{title}}`). This means `model.fancyTitle` will be inserted into an HTML string and rendered unescaped. The diff does not show any client-side escaping/sanitization at this point, so correctness/security depends on an external guarantee that `fancyTitle` is already sanitized server-side; that’s a real review concern introduced by this change, but the diff alone can’t prove it’s exploitable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:67 — unsubscribe_link` locale now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, so any MessageBuilder caller (plugins, custom mailers) that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument in both html_part and body.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `unsubscribe_link` in `config/locales/server.en.yml` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it unconditionally does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` without providing a default for `unsubscribe_url` or guarding its presence. Therefore, constructing a `MessageBuilder` with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but without `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at runtime (the spec was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, indicating the new requirement).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by` can return nil (user emailed via category watch/mention but never visited the topic), so `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError and the emailed link 500s.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level`. `find_by` can return `nil` (no `topic_users` row exists for that user/topic), which would raise `NoMethodError` and 500 the unsubscribe link. The diff does not create the `TopicUser` row before accessing it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — unsubscribe` is a state-mutating GET (mail clients/link prefetchers can trigger it) and returns the full topic-show JSON payload rather than a result status, with no confirmation step.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, wired via `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` (and `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`), and the action mutates state by toggling `TopicUser#notification_level` and calling `tu.save!`. Because it is a GET endpoint (and `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`), it can be triggered by link prefetchers/mail clients without explicit user intent and without CSRF-style protection typical for non-GET. It then calls `perform_show_response`, which renders the normal topic show HTML/JSON payload rather than a minimal status/confirmation response, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — Endpoint toggles rather than unsubscribes: a muted or regular user hitting the link is moved to `muted` and a tracking/watching user to `regular`, so repeated clicks produce different end states than the email link promises.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the logic explicitly toggles based on current `TopicUser.notification_level`: if `tu.notification_level > regular` it sets to `regular`, else it sets to `muted` (lines added in the diff under `def unsubscribe`). This means a watching/tracking user clicking an "unsubscribe" link is downgraded to `regular` rather than being definitively unsubscribed/muted, which conflicts with the email text added in `server.en.yml` ("To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic..."). The behavior is therefore a real, diff-grounded mismatch/defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:107 — List-Unsubscribe header still advertises `user_preferences_url` while the body now offers a per-topic unsubscribe URL; the machine-readable unsubscribe contract does not match the new per-topic option.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a per-topic `unsubscribe_url` into notification email template args (`user_notifications.rb` passes it; `server.en.yml` uses it in the body copy), but the shown changes in `lib/email/message_builder.rb` only affect HTML body substitution (`%{unsubscribe_link}`) and do not show any update to how the `List-Unsubscribe` header is constructed. The spec change also only asserts the header is present, not that it matches the new per-topic URL. So it’s a plausible mismatch/consistency concern introduced by this change, but it’s not verifiably a broken behavior from the diff alone (and it may be intentional for List-Unsubscribe to remain global).

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:437 — Redirecting a mutating endpoint with 301 (slug mismatch / missing slug) is cacheable by browsers; 302 is the conventional choice here.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the new action does `redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301` when the slug is missing/mismatched. This endpoint is a state-changing GET (it later toggles `TopicUser#notification_level`), so using a permanent (cacheable) redirect for canonicalization is a legitimate HTTP-semantics concern. The redirect happens before the mutation, so it’s not a direct correctness break, but it’s a concrete, diff-grounded behavior that a reviewer could reasonably flag.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/app-route-map.js.es6:13 — Ember route uses `:id` while Rails routes use `:topic_id`; the slug-less `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` form has no client counterpart and relies solely on the server 301 redirect.

adjudication.rationale: In the Ember router the dynamic segment name `:id` is internal to the client; it still produces the same URL shape (`/t/:slug/<number>/unsubscribe`) that Rails routes (`:topic_id`) match, so there’s no verifiable defect from the name difference. The slug-less Rails route (`/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`) is explicitly handled server-side by redirecting (301) to `topic.unsubscribe_url` when `params[:slug].blank?`, so it’s not “missing” behavior in a broken way; it’s an intentional server redirect path shown in `TopicsController#unsubscribe`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:438 — Removing the `post_number` constraint from summary routes is a no-op (no such segment) and reordering moderator-liked has no effect, but the unrelated churn widens the diff without stated intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show removal of a redundant `post_number` constraint on summary routes and a reorder of the `moderator-liked` route, but the finding is essentially a diff-churn/style nit (no functional issue is demonstrated by the diff itself). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:500 — Explicit `render :show` makes `unsubscribe` serve the full server-rendered topic page (crawler/no-JS view shows topic content, not an unsubscribe confirmation).
